newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks weaker, bearish trend seen lasting.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks weaker, bearish trend seen lasting.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mostly weaker on Wednesday in modest trade and market participants expected a bearish trend to persist through this week.
"Today was a disaster. There were fewer transactions and most shares fell," said one trader with a large market share. "We are not likely to see a strong recovery any time soon."
Josko Milisa, chief trader at I.C.F. brokerage, also saw no end to the current stagnation until foreign investors returned to the tiny market more aggressively.
Volume fell to 7,567 units from Tuesday's 11,386, with turnover rising very slightly to 5.6 million kuna.
Nine of 15 issues fell on Wednesday, five rose and one ended flat. Both blue chips Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka dipped.
Pliva lost six kuna or 1.24 percent to 478 kuna in two straight deals totalling 1,000 shares.
Zagrebacka's ordinaries fell 50 kuna or 2.3 percent to 2,150 kuna on volume of 1,632 units.
"In part this is an expected correction after too steep a rise, but it also follows a drop in London," said the first trader.
He referred to trade in Pliva's and Zagrebacka's global depositary receipts (GDRs) which nudged lower to $16 and $35.12 respectively.

But Milisa pointed out the bank's E-series preferred stock, rising 16 kuna to 1,099, for being less susceptiple to London price movements. Holders of these shares have a guaranteed dividend of seven percent on their 100-mark nominal price.
The third fully-listed firm Varazdinska Banka was not traded on Wednesday. Both its ordinary and bearer shares will be split and reissued at 100 kuna later this month.
Food stock Podravka with 2,919 units sold at an average 297 kuna was the day's most active issue. It lost 1.64 percent from Tuesday to close at 300 kuna.
Traders put this down to leaks about the firm's allegedly poor 1996 results, which are due to be released officially in 10-15 days.
"If (Podravka's) price goes below 300 kuna, the selling pressure could increase," one market watcher said.
Zagreb's Hotel Intercontinental led decliners, falling 11.76 percent since two weeks ago to 150 kuna on volume of 88 shares.
Top gainer was hotelier Arenaturist, up four kuna or 2.84 percent to 145 kuna on volume of 162 shares.
